records.description: Pure and domain-neutral shareability policy. It consumes artifact metadata and policy configuration only. It does not inspect or sanitize bytes, infer privacy facts, collect consent, export artifacts, contact a reviewer, or know an application, media domain, or destination service.
scenarios: As an artifact-policy consumer, I want an artifact to be shareable when its audience and sensitivity are allowed and required consent/sanitization are satisfied so that a host can enforce export policy consistently.

As an artifact-policy consumer, I want disallowed audiences, sensitivity classes, missing sanitization, or missing consent blocked or referred for review so that incomplete protection never silently authorizes sharing.

records.description:
core.authorize is a pure, side-effect-free authorization capability designed for maximum reusability across web, mobile, desktop, edge, and AI-agent runtimes.

It deliberately separates policy definition from policy evaluation. The caller supplies a complete, versioned policy configuration at invocation time (or a compact reference in future extensions). The same WASM binary can therefore enforce RBAC, ABAC, ReBAC-lite, hybrid, or explicit allow/deny rules without recompilation.

Key design principles (Persona-Council reviewed):
- Fail-closed by default (default_effect = deny).
- Fully deterministic: identical inputs always produce identical outputs.
- No host, network, or filesystem access.
- Structured, machine-readable output suitable for audit logs, UI enforcement, and downstream agents.
- Explicit support for multi-tenant isolation, hierarchical roles, time/context conditions, ownership, relationships, high-priority denies, and break-glass overrides.
- Obligations are first-class structured objects (not free-form strings) so callers know exactly what additional steps are required.

The capability never mutates state and never contacts external systems. All decision logic lives inside the supplied policy + the deterministic evaluator.

Known intentional limitations (disclosed):
- The evaluator implements a practical subset of common authorization patterns; it is not a full XACML or Cedar engine.
- Complex boolean expressions inside conditions are limited to a small, safe DSL to keep the WASM footprint and attack surface small.
- Policy size should be kept modest when inlined; very large policy sets should be versioned and referenced externally in future iterations.
scenarios: As a platform security engineer, I want an admin user with the correct role to be allowed to delete a document so that privileged operations succeed when policy permits them.
As a multi-tenant SaaS developer, I want a user to be denied access to a resource that belongs to a different tenant even if they hold a powerful role, so that tenant isolation is enforced.
As a collaboration product owner, I want the owner of a resource to always be able to update it, so that ownership rights are respected regardless of role.
As a security engineer, I want a high-priority explicit deny to override an allow rule so that a compromised or suspended account cannot exercise privileges.
As a compliance officer, I want an allow decision to carry structured obligations (require MFA + audit) so that the calling system can enforce additional controls.
As a developer, I want any request that matches no rule to be denied when default_effect is deny, so that the system fails closed.
As a runtime, I want an empty or malformed policy to always produce a deny with a clear reason_code so that invalid configurations cannot open the system.
As an incident responder, I want a break-glass flag to allow a temporary override while still recording that the override was used, so that emergency access is possible but fully auditable.
As a client developer, I want a clear structured denial when the principal object is missing required fields so that I can surface a precise error instead of a generic failure.
records.summary: Pure authorization evaluator: allow/deny for principal+action+resource under a caller-supplied versioned policy.

records.description:
Pure, deterministic decision procedure for consent and purpose binding evaluation (issue #500). Evaluates whether caller-supplied consent records allow a requested processing purpose for a subject under a caller-supplied policy version and evaluation timestamp (now). Never accesses external storage, clocks, connectors, or network.

Matching and evaluation semantics:
- Consents are evaluated in declaration order. The first record whose purpose exactly matches requested_purpose determines the decision and matched_consent_index.
- If status is 'withdrawn', decision is 'deny' with reason_code 'consent_withdrawn'.
- If status is 'denied', decision is 'deny' with reason_code 'consent_denied'.
- If status is 'granted', validity timestamps are evaluated: if granted_at > now or unparseable, fails closed with 'deny' / 'invalid_input'; if expires_at <= now, decision is 'deny' with 'consent_expired'; otherwise 'allow' with 'consent_granted'.
- If no record matches requested_purpose, decision is 'deny' with 'purpose_not_granted'.
- Malformed input fields or timestamps fail closed with 'deny' and 'invalid_input'.
- Scope intersection: v1.0.0 performs exact purpose matching; scope is preserved as metadata without filtering.
scenarios: As a compliance officer, I want a granted consent for the requested purpose to be allowed, so that lawful processing can proceed.
As a compliance officer, I want a withdrawn consent for the requested purpose to be denied, so that processing immediately ceases when consent is rescinded.
As a compliance officer, I want an explicitly denied consent for the requested purpose to be denied, so that opt-outs are strictly enforced.
As a compliance officer, I want an expired consent for the requested purpose to be denied, so that processing stops once the validity window closes.
As a compliance officer, I want a request with no matching consent purpose to be denied, so that unauthorized purposes fail closed by default.
As a runtime engineer, I want malformed timestamps to be rejected, so that corrupted inputs fail safely without guessing intent.
records.summary: Pure, deterministic consent and purpose binding check answering whether supplied consent data allows a requested purpose.

records.description:
Policy-driven comment processor for create/edit/reply/delete/react with mentions, quarantine, soft-delete, and tenant isolation.

Implemented and smoke-tested matrix (use_cases):
- create with @mention and https link + notify obligations
- edit denied when own_only and actor is not creator
- reply denied when parent_depth+1 >= max_thread_depth
- create allowed with quarantine when body matches moderation.blocklist
- react add normalized to a reaction set
- soft-delete retains body and records deleted_by
- create denied on tenant mismatch
- create/edit/reply denied for empty/whitespace body
- body_too_long when body exceeds max_body_length
- invalid_reaction when react lacks emoji
- insufficient_role when actor role not permitted

Known limitations (intentional in 1.2.0):
- resolve / unresolve / pin / unpin are not part of the schema surface
- mention_resolution narrowed to strict; permissive/disabled removed
- visibility_model narrowed to resource-acl|channel
- reaction.op narrowed to add (remove not published)
- invalid_action / invalid_parent / policy_error / not_authorized removed from published reason_code vocabulary
- hard_delete_unsupported and invalid_input/invalid_actor fail-closed paths exist but are not published reason_codes
- allowed_markups is accepted but body markup is not sanitized
- The capability never persists data or sends notifications; callers must honor obligations

On decision=allow, the WASM guest calls traverse_host::emit_event for core.comment.processed@1.0.0 with payload {action, actor_id, resource_type, resource_id, reason_code, comment_id}.
scenarios: As a collaboration platform engineer, I want a user to create a top-level comment with mentions so that the system receives a fully validated, sanitized comment object ready for persistence and notification.
As a security architect, I want an edit attempt by a non-owner to be denied when the policy requires own_only, so that users cannot modify other people's comments.
As a collaboration platform engineer, I want a reply that would exceed the configured max_thread_depth to be rejected so that threads cannot grow unbounded.
As a content moderation specialist, I want a comment containing a blocklisted term to be allowed only with a quarantine obligation so that moderators can review it before it becomes widely visible.
As a client developer, I want adding a reaction to be an idempotent, atomic action that returns the updated reaction set so that the UI can optimistically update without race conditions.
As a compliance officer, I want a soft-delete to preserve the original body and record who deleted it so that eDiscovery remains possible.
As a multi-tenant platform engineer, I want a cross-tenant comment attempt to be denied even if the user has the correct role, so that tenant isolation is absolute.
As a client developer, I want an empty or whitespace-only body to be rejected with a clear reason code so that the UI can show an inline validation error.
As a client developer, I want a body exceeding max_body_length rejected with body_too_long, so that oversized comments fail with a precise code.
As a client developer, I want a react without emoji rejected with invalid_reaction, so that malformed reactions never update the set.
As a security architect, I want create denied with insufficient_role when the actor role is not permitted, so that role gates stay enforceable.
records.summary: Policy-driven comment processor for create/edit/reply/delete/react with mentions, quarantine, soft-delete, and tenant isolation.

records.description: Pure model-neutral policy planning. Consumes trusted evidence labels from an authorized verifier and explicit target/runtime compatibility and memory facts. It neither verifies signatures or digests nor fetches, selects, downloads, caches, executes, or activates an artifact. Runtime remains responsible for independently enforcing activation authority.
scenarios: As a model-runtime policy consumer, I want a compatible artifact with verified provenance, accepted licence evidence, and sufficient memory to receive an activation plan so that runtime-specific activation can remain separate from portable policy.

As a model-runtime policy consumer, I want target, memory, failed evidence, and unknown-evidence cases rejected or escalated according to explicit policy so that unsupported or unverifiable artifacts are not silently approved.
As a model-runtime policy consumer, I want failed digest, signature, licence, or compatibility evidence to reject an activation plan so that every negative evidence state is explicit and testable.

As a model-runtime policy consumer, I want unknown signature, licence, and compatibility evidence to follow the configured reject action so that incomplete verification cannot be mistaken for approval.
records.summary: Create a model activation eligibility plan from verified evidence and configurable runtime policy.

records.description: Pure generic policy planner. Converts an eligibility classification into no action or a configured archive/delete plan with explicit grace period and approval state. It never deletes, archives, reads, or writes assets. The host must re-check holds and references at execution time, require approval when specified, and invoke the separately authorized storage connector.
scenarios: As a retention steward, I want an eligible asset to receive a delayed archive or deletion plan according to policy so that retention actions are auditable and not immediate side effects.
As a retention steward, I want held or retained assets to produce no action, and eligible plans to fail on time overflow, so that protected data is not scheduled for removal.
As a retention steward, I want an asset already retained under policy to produce no archive or delete plan so that retained data is not actioned a second time.
records.summary: Create a delayed, approval-aware retention action plan without executing it.

records.description: Applies the standard Luhn (mod 10) checksum algorithm to a digit string: doubling every second digit from the rightmost, subtracting 9 from any result over 9, summing all digits, and checking the total is a multiple of 10. This is a checksum-format check only -- it does NOT verify the number belongs to a real, active account, is not stolen, or is authorized for any transaction (none of that is possible without a live call to a card network or issuer, which is not available to any capability under the current ABI whitelist). Luhn validity is necessary but nowhere near sufficient for treating a card number as safe to charge. Formatting characters (spaces, dashes) are stripped before checking when strip_formatting is true (the default); the input is never logged, persisted, or included in the output.
scenarios: As a checkout flow developer, I want a well-formed card number with spaces or dashes to still pass the Luhn checksum, so that a customer who types their card number with natural formatting isn't wrongly rejected.
As a checkout flow developer, I want a single mistyped digit to fail the Luhn checksum, so that I can catch an obvious card-number typo before submitting a doomed charge attempt.
As a checkout flow developer, I want an empty string to be rejected before any checksum math runs, so that a blank card-number field fails fast with a clear reason instead of an ambiguous result.
records.summary: Check whether a numeric string passes the Luhn checksum, as used by credit card numbers and other identifiers.

entrypoint.description:
Pure authorization evaluator: allow/deny for principal+action+resource under a caller-supplied versioned policy (RBAC/hybrid rule matching, tenant/status conditions, break-glass, obligations).

Implemented and smoke-tested matrix (use_cases):
- admin role allow (matched_allow_rule)
- tenant isolation deny (matched_deny_rule)
- owner update allow (matched_allow_rule)
- suspended principal deny (matched_deny_rule)
- allow with obligations (matched_allow_rule)
- no matching rule → deny (no_matching_rule)
- empty policy rules → empty_or_invalid_policy
- break-glass override (break_glass_override)
- missing principal.id → invalid_principal
- missing action → invalid_action
- missing resource.type → invalid_resource

- policy.mode values abac/explicit removed from schema (not distinct evaluator modes in this binary)
- default_effect narrowed to deny (fail-closed); allow-default not published

- condition_failed / policy_evaluation_error are not emitted as distinct reason_codes
- Condition DSL is a practical subset (eq/neq on selected attribute paths), not full XACML/Cedar

scenarios: As a platform security engineer, I want an admin user with the correct role to be allowed to delete a document so that privileged operations succeed when policy permits them.
As a multi-tenant SaaS developer, I want a user to be denied access to a resource that belongs to a different tenant even if they hold a powerful role, so that tenant isolation is enforced.
As a collaboration product owner, I want the owner of a resource to always be able to update it, so that ownership rights are respected regardless of role.
As a security engineer, I want a high-priority explicit deny to override an allow rule so that a compromised or suspended account cannot exercise privileges.
As a compliance officer, I want an allow decision to carry structured obligations (require MFA + audit) so that the calling system can enforce additional controls.
As a developer, I want any request that matches no rule to be denied when default_effect is deny, so that the system fails closed.
As a runtime, I want an empty or malformed policy to always produce a deny with a clear reason_code so that invalid configurations cannot open the system.
As an incident responder, I want a break-glass flag to allow a temporary override while still recording that the override was used, so that emergency access is possible but fully auditable.
As a client developer, I want a clear structured denial when the principal object is missing required fields so that I can surface a precise error instead of a generic failure.
As a client developer, I want missing action rejected with invalid_action, so that callers can fix request shape without guessing.
As a client developer, I want missing resource.type rejected with invalid_resource, so that incomplete resource descriptors fail closed.
